cards.front: Recall a key point about Depth Study Technique
cards.back: The Depth Study (Paper 2) is worth 50% of the GCSE and lasts 1 hour 30 minutes

cards.front: Recall a key point about Depth Study Technique
cards.back: It focuses on a shorter period in much greater detail, requiring depth of knowledge and source analysis

cards.front: Recall a key point about Depth Study Technique
cards.back: Source-based questions are central to the Depth Study — you must use sources as evidence

cards.front: Recall a key point about Depth Study Technique
cards.back: The paper may ask you to evaluate the utility of a source for a specific question

cards.front: Recall a key point about Depth Study Technique
cards.back: You may be asked to compare two sources or interpretations, identifying agreement and disagreement

cards.front: Recall a key point about Depth Study Technique
cards.back: Interpretation questions ask you to explain why historians might disagree about an event or person

cards.front: Recall a key point about Depth Study Technique
cards.back: For source questions, always combine what the source says with your own contextual knowledge

cards.front: Recall a key point about Depth Study Technique
cards.back: The Depth Study rewards depth of knowledge — detailed, precise evidence about a narrower period

cards.front: Recall a key point about Depth Study Technique
cards.back: When evaluating interpretations, consider what evidence the historian used and what they might have omitted

cards.front: Recall a key point about Depth Study Technique
cards.back: Depth Study topics include: Sparta, Athens, the foundation of Rome, or the Roman Emperors

cards.front: Recall a key point about Depth Study Technique
cards.back: Always refer to the source by name or provenance, not just 'the source says'

cards.front: Recall a key point about Depth Study Technique
cards.back: The extended question in the Depth Study usually involves evaluating a claim or interpretation using evidence

cards.front: What should you know about gcse ancient history exam tips — depth study technique?
cards.back: 1. For Depth Study Technique, include specific factual detail: dates, names, events and statistics where relevant 2. For source questions, analyse provenance (who, when, why, audience) before using the content 3. In evaluation questions, discuss multiple factors and weigh their relative significance 4. Always link back to the question focus — don't just narrate what happened with Depth Study Technique 5. Use phrases like 'the most significant factor was... because...' to show analytical judgement
